Name: Ant Pour Over Set
Desc: Know the Artist This is a product of collaboration with Zarava, a pottery and ceramic studio based out of Mysore, Karnataka. They handcraft and produce some exceptional tableware! Know the Pour Over This Pour Over set is dense, heavy and wholesome to hold. It truly complements the kind of brew that a pour over produces too – intentional, precise, mild and clean! Being slightly on the giant side of the spectrum, these mugs can be saved for mornings that demand a larger dose of coffee than usual. This charmingly crafted ceramic set is sparsely populated with hand-painted ants. A pleasing addition to your kitchen and coffee counters, the white is sure to bring light and brightness into the space. The Pour Over weights 500g and the mug 400g. They both hold 300 ml of liquid. They are made such that the Hario V-60 paper filters will work but we strongly recommend that you use our handloom cloth filters. Better for the earth! Pour Over grinds range from Medium Fine, Medium to Medium Coarse. If you're using a cloth filter, your drip down time could be faster, so do try a shade finer than you usually would. These are handmade, each pour over is slightly different. Each Pour Over set comes with 2 of our special handloom cloth filters.

Name: Cascara
Desc: Know the Cascara Cascara tastes nothing like coffee! The word, Cascara which can be translated from Spanish to mean "husk", is an increasingly popular byproduct of coffee processing. After coffee fruit is picked and pulped, the fruity pulp is dried to produce cascara, also known as dried coffee cherries. Our version is slightly tweaked, it is cascara in its original form, the husk of fruit after both have been dried together. Cascara can be brewed like loose leaf tea, steeped in hot water or as a cold brew. Although it does contain caffeine, it is about a quarter of that of coffee and jampacked with antioxidants. We love coffee but we're nudging you to try a lesser known part of coffee's journey! Know the Grower The Arabica from which this Cascara comes, has been grown by our partner producers in Biligirirangan Hills. This region, BRT as it is fondly known is a magnificent forest with elevational gradients that go from 800 to 1600m! This unique range in altitude enables all major forest types and this in turn produces a magical cup of coffee...and cascara! How to Use You can enjoy both hot and cold brew versions. Here is our recommended recipe: Cascara Tonic: Ingredients: 1 tbsp C ascara 3 cups Water 2 tbsp Jaggery Tonic Water Lime Ice Method: Simmer the Cascara, water and jaggery on medium heat for about 10-15 minutes till the volume is reduced to half. Allow it to cool, strain the mixture, and refrigerate. To make the Cascara Tonic, add ice cubes into a tall glass, pour 90 ml of the Cascara brew, the juice of half a lime and top with tonic water. Garnish with a slice of lime. Developed in partnership with The Locavore & Chef Thomas Zacharias

Name: Heavy Lies The Grain
Tasting_Notes: WHEN 13 March 2026, 6:00 – 7:00 PM WHERE Black Baza
Desc: WHEN 13 March 2026 | 6:00 – 7:00 PM WHERE Black Baza Roastery, Sahakaranagar, Bangalore HEAVY LIES THE GRAIN What does Punjab’s current agricultural landscape reveal about the human and environmental toll of India’s Green Revolution? While the program saved millions from hunger, decades of chemical-intensive monocropping have left fractured soils, depleted water systems, and taken a heavy toll on farmers’ lives. Since 2016, photojournalist Harsha Vadlamani has been travelling across Punjab, documenting the Green Revolution’s complex legacy. Join us as he showcases his photographs and reflects on the many layers of contemporary Punjab. LIVING RESPONSIBLY ON THE PLANET Through conversations, collaborations, and community engagements, we explore what it means to tread lighter and live consciously in a warming, changing world. These gatherings are as much about our own learning as sharing ideas — an invitation to reflect, question, and figure things out together. If you’re curious, join us.

Desc: WHEN 6 March 2026 | 6:00 – 7:00 PM WHERE Black Baza Roastery, Sahakaranagar, Bangalore GETTING ROASTED IN BANGALORE Bangalore's climate is cited as one of the cities greatest benefits, but does that climate even exist anymore? The Ant Loop Set
Desc: The Ant Loop Gift Box A stunning gift box for ant lovers, someone discovering coffee...or just a collector of one-of-a-kind brewing equipment! Our pitch is for gifts that are kinder to the planet! This gift box has no plastic packaging, is beautifully presented and designed for both somebody discovering coffee and for someone who appreciates traditional craftsmanship in their coffee brewing equipment. The brass filter coffee is a uniquely South Asian coffee brewing technique which involves a fairly slow percolation of finely ground coffee in a traditional filter. The result is a heavy bodied and rich brew that is delicious both hot or as an iced version. Gift Sustainably: If you'd like to customise gift boxes with bulk discounts, please fill out this form below and someone from our team will reach out to you: Inquiry for Sustainable Gifting Why Ants? Because, to grow good coffee, one needs ants! Ants are remarkable indicators of ecological health in coffee farms because they play essential roles in pest control, soil aeration, and nutrient cycling. Their presence often signals a balanced ecosystem, as they keep pest populations in check and contribute to the soil's richness. By studying ant diversity, we get insights into the farm’s overall biodiversity, showing how interconnected and resilient the environment truly is. Plus, they're funny, cute little creatures with fascinating social structures, making them fab mascots for sustainable farming! Here’s an ode to ants: our coffee companions all the way from farms right up to our kitchen counters! The Contents Ant Loop Gift Box: - 100g of coffee of your choice* - Ant Loop Brass Filter - Ant Loop Brass Tumbler Set *If you forget to mention this, we'll send you our Whistling Schoolboy coffee. This coffee is only available as a Medium Fine grind. If you would like Whole Bean, select a different coffee! Optional Add-Ons: - Brass Tumbler Set - Wooden Ant Scoop - Ant Tote Bag - Ceramic Ant Pour Over - Ceramic Ant Mug - 100g

Name: Coffee & Coex-hiss-tence
Tasting_Notes: WHEN 20 September 2025, 4 PM WHERE Black Baza
Desc: WHEN 20 September 2025 | 4 PM WHERE Black Baza Roastery, Sahakaranagar, Bangalore Gnaneswar Ch is joining us at the Black Baza Coffee Roastery to take us into the world of snakes. An early-career conservationist with a deep fondness for reptiles, he leads the Snakebite Mitigation Project at the Madras Crocodile Bank Trust and works across research, education, and policy to reduce human–snake conflict. Join us for an evening of coffee and conversation as Gnaneswar breaks down myths, shares stories from the field, and guides us through hands-on activities to understand what coexistence with snakes really looks like.

Name: Nuts Over Coffee
Tasting_Notes: WHEN 13 September 2025, 10 AM WHERE Black Baza
Desc: WHEN 13 September 2025 | 10 AM WHERE Black Baza Roastery, Sahakaranagar, Bangalore We’re brewing up something nutty! The Australian Macadamia Society and Black Baza Coffee are teaming up for the Australian Macadamia Festival 2025 with 'Nuts for Coffee' — a conversation that brings coffee and macadamias to the same table, with sustainability at its heart. Cracking into new ideas and flavours, we’ll be joined by Clare Hamilton-Bate, CEO of the Australian Macadamia Society (AMS), in conversation with our founder, Arshiya Bose. Together, they’ll explore how macadamias and coffee share roots in sustainable, community-led farming, and the exciting possibilities that lie ahead. And the best part? You get to taste it for yourself! As more people look for planet-friendly dairy alternatives, macadamia nut mylk is making its mark — creamy, delicious, and sustainable. After the talk, we’ll be serving macadamia nut mylk coffee for you to try. Reserve your spot!

Name: Toadally Fascinating!
Tasting_Notes: WHEN 29 August 2025, 6 PM WHERE Black Baza
Desc: WHEN 29 August 2025 | 6 PM WHERE Black Baza Roastery, Sahakaranagar, Bangalore Dr. Seshadri K. S. is joining us at the Black Baza Coffee roastery to take us into the world of amphibians. From watching sparrows nest in his childhood courtyard to being awarded the 'Future Conservationist' award for his research into the amphibian world of the Western Ghats, he has spent a lifetime hopping through nature, discovering new species along the way. Join us for an evening of conversations and coffee as Dr. Seshadri helps us appreciate the curious lives of frogs and toads, and has us play The Happy Frog, a board game designed to make people more aware of their world!

Name: Gooseneck Kettle
Desc: Know the Artist The artist, Kalabati Majumdar has created thoughtful depictions of the interconnectedness between coffee producers, coffee farms and the ecosystem. These enamel coffee mugs are our first foray into the world of 'merchandise' but perhaps more importantly, a daily reminder we need to be mindful of our footsteps and footprints on the natural world...and that change is possible, one cup at a time. Know Enamel This enamel coffee mug is crafted from solid iron and then carefully coated with enamel. An intriguing historical fact is that enameling traces its origins back to the Mesopotamian civilization, originally developed for jewelry making! The mug can hold approximately 350 ml, and is not microwave or dishwasher-safe. While robust and resistant to shattering upon impact, repeated damage may result in minor cracks on the enamel coating. Each mug is handmade, imbuing it with a unique character, so each mug could be slightly different in appearance.

Name: Shared with Elephants
Tasting_Notes: WHEN 6PM, Friday, 31 January 2025 WHERE Black Baza
Desc: WHEN 6PM, Friday, 31 January 2025 WHERE Black Baza Roastery, Sahakaranagar, Bangalore Ever imagined living and farming amidst the wild? Well, with ‘development’ creeping into natural spaces, an elephant in your backyard might not be too far from reality soon. As human and animal habitats intertwine, finding innovative ways to coexist has never been more urgent. Our speakers for the day have been working together on the ground since 2016, paving the way for harmony between humans and animals through thoughtful collaboration. Join us as Anandram Reddy , a millet-and-mango farmer living adjacent to the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu, and Nishant Srinivasaiah , a behavioural ecologist, take us through their experiences of innovating practical ways to address human-elephant conflict, reduce crop losses and improve farmer livelihoods! You’ll also get a taste of Anand’s farm-fresh produce with a delicious mini Ragi Mudde and Huruli Saaru — and of course, no event would be complete without Black Baza coffee!

Name: The Dirt on Packaging Waste
Desc: WHEN 4:30 PM, Saturday, 8 March 2025 WHERE Mystery Venue Near Ulsoor (RSVP to find out!) Ever wondered what happens to your trash after you toss it in the bin? Does recycling actually work? Is compostable packaging as sustainable as it seems? And where does all that waste go? Join us on 8th March at 4:30 PM for an evening of coffee and conversations with Karthik Natarajan, a multidisciplinary researcher with over five years in the waste management space. Together, we’ll unpack the many layers of product packaging and what happens once it leaves our hands. Of course, no Black Baza Coffee event is complete without coffee — we’ll serve up a  cold brew! We’re hosting this at a secret venue that sets the perfect stage for this conversation — RSVP to find out! (Don’t worry, it’s close to Ulsoor and Central Bangalore, so getting there will be a breeze.)

Name: Steeping Stories
Tasting_Notes: WHEN 4:30 PM, Saturday, 10 May 2025 WHERE Black Baza
Desc: WHEN 4:30 PM, Saturday, 10 May 2025 WHERE Black Baza Roastery, Sahakaranagar, Bangalore We’re hosting a special tasting at the roastery—and you’re invited! The Sugarcane Ferment is here — a microlot that reflects Veeramma and Chikanna’s drive to experiment, innovate, and bring something truly unique to your cup. This post-harvest adventure is full of unexpected flavour and possibility, and we can’t wait to share it with our #BlackBazaCommunity. You’ll get to taste the coffee, hear the story behind it, and for those curious to brew better — we’re also running a short pour over session to guide you through the process. And to keep things cool, we’ll be serving our sugarcane cascara tonic — a summer favourite! Spots are limited—RSVP via the link in bio!

Name: Connections, Naturally
Tasting_Notes: WHEN 6:00 PM, Friday, 16 May 2025 WHERE Black Baza
Desc: WHEN 6:00 PM, Friday, 16 May 2025 WHERE Black Baza Roastery, Sahakaranagar, Bangalore It's a real privilege to catch Karthik for a quick evening between his wildlife travels around the world. Karthik will share stories about connections in the natural world - through a series of compelling examples, many featuring the Black Baza cadre of species you are all already so familiar with! He will gently unravel the threads that bind ecosystems together and sustain life across them. It’s a ticketed event with limited seats — head to the link in our bio to RSVP before they’re gone! The ticket price is fully redeemable against purchases at the store.

Name: Follow The Light
Tasting_Notes: WHEN 4:30 PM, Saturday, 19 July 2025 WHERE Black Baza
Desc: WHEN 4:30 PM, Saturday, 19 July 2025 WHERE Black Baza Roastery, Sahakaranagar, Bangalore Join us for an evening of coffee and conversation as Pritha illuminates the fascinating world of moths. With a PhD in moth taxonomy and diversity, she’s spent much of her life exploring a world that often goes unnoticed — and she’s going to show us how we can too. From setting up light traps to photographing and recording species, Pritha will walk us through how anyone — whether you're just curious or already deep into nature — can tune into the hidden world of nocturnal biodiversity. It’s a ticketed event with limited seats — head to the link in our bio to RSVP before they’re gone! The ticket price is fully redeemable against purchases at the store.

Name: Anaerobic Naturals
Desc: Coffee Arabica Anaerobic Naturals During this year's harvest, our team worked closely with two producer families to produce this surprising coffee. We carried out an extended fermentation over a period of 96 hours in closed, anaerobic conditions of coffee fruit, and the result is a jammy jackfruit flavour profile! FLAVOUR NOTES: Ripe Jackfruit BREW: Pour Over RECIPE: For a pour over, place a filter in your dripper and rinse with hot water to eliminate the taste of paper. Add 15g of medium-ground coffee. Pour 250ml of hot water (92-94°C) in slow, circular motions, starting from the centre and moving outward, allowing the coffee to bloom, and continue pouring until the desired amount of water has passed through. NOTE: The 'best brewed with' list suggests methods for the best cup, but isn’t restrictive—this coffee can be ground and brewed however you prefer. Meet the Grower ORIGIN: BR Hills, Karnataka GROWER: Madevi, Madammma, Basavanna and Madegowda ABOUT: In a remote hamlet nestled deep within the BR Hills Tiger Reserve, family members and neighbours—our partner producers—took a bold risk with this coffee. They watched with equal parts patience and nervousness as freshly picked coffee cherries turned from bright red to deep purple, slowly fermenting without air. Their young children and a mischievous baby goat named Ganesha offered a welcome distraction during those tense, uncertain days. PRICE PAID IN 2025: Rs 1000/kg ~ $11.8/kg for equivalent green coffee 2.4x the Fair Trade minimum price Our price isn’t driven by speculative markets but reflects quality and the growers' commitment to biodiversity-friendly farming. Our higher price floor ensures a more sustainable income for farmers. Name: Coffee Sampler Pack
Desc: Know the Coffee The Sampler Pack allows you to try the amazing diversity of coffees we grow, roast and blend. You can expect to find the flavours of Western Ghats coffee in one box! So go for it! Try and Arabicas, blends of Arabicas and Robustas and the straight up Robustas all before you make up your mind. Why not? Even better, try and cup taste these coffees blind! And then come back, tell us which one you like and let's make that your regular! Know the Growers The coffees in this Sampler Pack come from all of the regions we work in: BR Hills in Karnataka, The Nilgiris in Tamil Nadu, Kodagu in Karnataka and Wayanad in Kerala. The Contents The Sampler Pack contains: 1. WANDEROO | MEDIUM ROAST, 100g 2. JUMPING ANT | LIGHT ROAST, 100g 3. FICUS | MEDIUM-DARK ROAST, 100g 4. OTTER | MEDIUM DARK ROAST, 100g 5. LUNA | DARK ROAST, 100g 6. WHISTLING SCHOOLBOY | MEDIUM-DARK ROAST, MEDIUM-FINE GRIND, 100g *Disclaimer:* The Whistling Schoolboy comes pre-ground in a medium-fine grind because that’s how roasted chicory arrives at our HQ! Another disclaimer: If you prefer coffee without our chicory blend, please drop us a note and we will send you another coffee.

Name: Lactic Process
Desc: Meet the Producers of Lactic Wash We are continuously inspired by our partner producers – especially those who choose to take fermentation risks with us! We want to acknowledge the courage it takes to try out a new coffee processing technique. In most cases, the producers of our Microlots, like this Lactic Process, are the first people in their hamlets to have ever tried out these methods and we can't wait for you to try it! Let us know what you think and we'll pass on your feedback. Producers: Madegowda, Masthegowda & Basamma, BR Hills You've tried Lactobacillus in curd but have you in coffee? This diverse group of bacteria is abundant in nature, inside our bodies and in our food. In post-harvest processing of coffee, sugary coffee fruits are kept in anaerobic conditions such that the LAB bacteria can eat away at all the sugars. This fermentation produces metabolites that are then absorbed by the coffee beans to produce flavour. Many microorganisms ferment coffee fruit, but through close monitoring of pH, temperature and oxygen availability, we can create environmental conditions that preferentially allow LAB to thrive. Carrying out controlled fermentations is complex - there are many variables to account for and there is no set recipe for a lactic process coffee. Pushing a lactic fermentation can result in overly bitter cups whereas if you get it right, your brew could be buttery, fruity and floral. This was our first collective attempt at a Lactic Process. Full disclosure, we're happy-ish and think that we perhaps need to modify the fermentation time for future experiments. The coffee is delicious, despite all challenges, and we're very happy to be sharing it with you! Flavour Notes: Molasses, Clove & Dried Fruit Recommended Brewing: Pourover & Drip Filter AeroPress : Use a Medium or Medium Coarse Grind, 1:15 ratio and start with 15g, use 2 paper filters or 1 of our cloth filters.

Name: Lactic Process
Desc: Meet the Producers of Lactic Wash We are continuously inspired by our partner producers – especially those who choose to take fermentation risks with us! We want to acknowledge the courage it takes to try out a new coffee processing technique. In most cases, the producers of our Microlots, like this Lactic Process, are the first people in their hamlets to have ever tried out these methods and we can't wait for you to try it! Let us know what you think and we'll pass on your feedback. Producers: Madegowda, Masthegowda & Basamma, BR Hills You've tried Lactobacillus in curd but have you in coffee? This diverse group of bacteria is abundant in nature, inside our bodies and in our food. In post-harvest processing of coffee, sugary coffee fruits are kept in anaerobic conditions such that the LAB bacteria can eat away at all the sugars. This fermentation produces metabolites that are then absorbed by the coffee beans to produce flavour. Many microorganisms ferment coffee fruit, but through close monitoring of pH, temperature and oxygen availability, we can create environmental conditions that preferentially allow LAB to thrive. Carrying out controlled fermentations is complex - there are many variables to account for and there is no set recipe for a lactic process coffee. Name: Microlot 36 | Anaerobic Fermentation of Washed Arabica
Desc: Monthly Microlots We do Microlots because Indian coffee is simply far too diverse and heterogenous to standardise flavour profiles from coffee beans, especially where the, geographical, sociocultural and ecological life histories of these coffees is so different. Since we work directly with so many smallholder producers, we end up with many beautiful but very small, experimental lots of coffee. Find them here! Microlot 36 | Anaerobic Fermentation of Washed Arabica For Microlot 36, we chose to work with washed Arabica. A very special and small lot is anaerobically fermented in Maadhegowda’s farm in the deciduous forests of BR Hills, at the confluence of the eastern and western ghats. We must mention and expand on the microclimate at play, because it’s critical in allowing and influencing the diversity of microbes that can exist - in that controlled environment within a container in the absence of oxygen. Post the fermentation stage, untimely rains or the lack of them dictate the length of coffee drying periods as well as the amount of care and scrutiny required. No clear distinction in seasons, as years pass by, is also a factor and cause of uncertainty. We dried these fermented and washed beans for 10-11 days. Post two months of green beans resting, we roasted them light medium. The flavour profile: Peach-like sweet acidity, light hibiscus with a strong aroma. Earl grey tea-like body and finish. Recommended Brewing: This one is best brewed with an Aeropress and Pour over. It works surprisingly well on a French press too!

Name: Black Baza Stickers
Desc: Know the Stickers We're pleased that a fanbase for our coffees exist and this feeling spills into the species they're named after. So we created these adhesive embellishments - stickers, to help you express. Treat this as a badge of honour to be part of the community, if you will! They'll surely make nice additions to your unique sticker/ coffee merch collection. These miniature pieces also make for cute gifts :) These vinyls stick well on most surfaces (exceptions: rough, bumpy, uneven, rugged etc), they're water resistant, so don't be afraid to stick them on your coffee equipment or anywhere else in the kitchen! They're great in quality and will retain their vibrancy for a long time. Eventual and unwitting fading will occur with years passing. All stickers carry either our logo or website address on the outline. Our bigger stickers are in dimensions of about 7 cm x 7.5 cm, and smaller ones are sized around the average of 4.5 cm x 5.5 cm.

Name: Coffee Mug
Desc: Know the Artist The artist, Kalabati Majumdar has created thoughtful depictions of the interconnectedness between coffee producers, coffee farms and the ecosystem. These enamel coffee mugs are our first foray into the world of 'merchandise' but perhaps more importantly, a daily reminder we need to be mindful of our footsteps and footprints on the natural world...and that change is possible, one cup at a time. Know Enamel This enamel coffee mug is crafted from solid iron and then carefully coated with enamel. An intriguing historical fact is that enameling traces its origins back to the Mesopotamian civilization, originally developed for jewelry making! The mug can hold approximately 350 ml, and is not microwave or dishwasher-safe. While robust and resistant to shattering upon impact, repeated damage may result in minor cracks on the enamel coating. Each mug is handmade, imbuing it with a unique character, so each mug could be slightly different in appearance.

Name: Coffee Canister
Desc: Know the Artist The artist, Kalabati Majumdar has created thoughtful depictions of the interconnectedness between coffee producers, coffee farms and the ecosystem. These enamel canisters are our first foray into the world of 'merchandise' but perhaps more importantly, a daily reminder we need to be mindful of our footsteps and footprints on the natural world...and that change is possible, one cup at a time. Know Enamel This coffee canister is made of stainless steel, which has then been subjected to the ancient process of enamelling. It’s interesting to note that enamelling dates as far back as the Mesopotamian civilisation and was a technique developed for jewellery! Our previously much-loved canisters deserved a second edition! This one is slightly bigger than the original green canister and can hold little over 600g whole bean. These are not microwave or dishwasher-safe. Although this canister is sturdy and it will not shatter into pieces if dropped, it will show small cracks in the enamel coat from repeated damage. Heavy duty so your cute+aggressive pets cannot destroy, safe to store their treats in it! These are handmade, each enamel canister is slightly different.

Name: Chukki
Desc: Meet the Coffee This coffee is a Vienna Roast, dry ferment of carefully picked, sorted, pulped and washed Arabica. It was dry fermented in a barrel with pulped Arabica for 36 hours. While roasting, we particularly extended our development time on this one. The result is a brew with tasting notes of dark chocolate, roasted almonds and lingering caramel. This is best brewed with an Aeropress and Moka pot. Enjoy it black or with milk! Meet the Grower This beautiful Arabica coffee comes from our partner producers in the Biligirirangan Hills of Karnataka. This collective of growers is dreaming big about the wellbeing of their community and we are equally committed to enabling them to find their way. BR Hills is a magnificent forested landscape with elevational gradients that go from 800 to 1600m! This unique range in altitude enables all major forest types and this in turn produces a magical cup of coffee! Who's Chukki? Kethegowda decided where to set the camera trap - at the perimeter his coffee farm shares with the forest. She’s not the first Leopard we’ve spotted, but certainly is one that takes delight in making repeated visits to Kethegowda’s farm. The camera has been able to spot and capture her least once every month since the set-up. After a short, but happening discussion we decided to name her Chukki. Thanks to their cautious and elusive behaviour, we are yet to encounter one in daylight, despite sharing the neighbourhood. They’re usually active and preying at night. Being an apex predator makes the Leopard an indispensable part of the food chain and ecological balance of the region and the planet. Their continuous survival requires an abundance of prey and forest cover. Their population is mostly threatened by habitat loss from forest fragmentation. This gives us more reason to remain committed to growing coffee in the way that we do - under the canopy of native, moist deciduous forest trees and not despite it! Environment conditions that allow these leopards

Name: Black Baza Tote Bags
Desc: Know the Tote We have been carrying around these tote bags *everywhere* to put them through the ultimate tests - can they hold 15' laptops and notebooks, swimming gear, AeroPress and coffee paraphernalia, 3 kilos of mangoes, 1 kilo of rice and toor dal...You get the point! This bag holds all of the above and with such delicious comfort! We deliberately designed this bag with strong, long handles to be able to carry weight. All Tote Bag designs carry our signature emblem and logo on one side. Know Canvas These tote bags are made from canvas, we chose canvas over other alternative materials simply because canvas is so darn durable. Canvas is a plainly woven cotton fabric used to make boat sails, tents, shelters, shoes and backpacks. This fabric is not very breathable, so don't wear your tote bag! While canvas can be washed, we do not recommend washing this particular tote bag as the artwork will run.

Name: Biligiri Black Pepper
Tasting_Notes: Know the Pepper Biligiri Black Pepper is a spicy, fruity pepper from the the forests of BR Hills, Karnataka
Desc: Know the Pepper Biligiri Black Pepper is a spicy, fruity pepper from the the forests of BR Hills, Karnataka. This black pepper is vine-ripened, harvested by hand and has never seen the nozzle of a chemical sprayer or fertiliser. Please note that we will not grind this pepper for you! It is best stored as whole pepper! Know the Growers For half a decade, our partner coffee growers have nudged us to venture into pepper. Across the Western Ghats, coffee is intercropped with pepper and most of our partner coffee producers depend almost as seriously on pepper for their source of livelihood. What can we say, we are slow and organic and it has taken us longer than it should have to do our very first lot of this incredible spice! This particular crop comes from BR Hills, and grows alongside our high altitude and shade-grown Arabicas.

Name: Cloth Filters for AeroPress
Tasting_Notes: Cotton filters produce a clean, sediment-free cup of coffee with heavy aromatics and a buttery mouthfeel from natural
Desc: Why Handloom, not Paper! These handloom coffee filters are made from kora (unbleached & undyed) cotton yarn of 60’s x 40’s count. Cotton filters produce a clean, sediment-free cup of coffee with heavy aromatics and a buttery mouthfeel from natural oils and a higher perceived acidity in the brew. Once used, the cloth filter must be washed thoroughly with water only and left to air dry. We have used each cloth filter for over a hundred times before repurposing. In comparison, paper filters are more tightly woven, clean out most sediments and natural oils so your cup of coffee is clean but diminished in aromatic oils. They are also not reusable and as a result, high waste (both in terms of household waste as well in the use of trees at the paper mill). Fabrics of Resilience These handloom coffee filters celebrate local community and resilience in a time of crisis. The fabric that makes up these filters comes from the award winning organisation, Dastkar Andhra who have been working to revive handloom weaving in the villages of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh for many decades. The stitching of the cloth filters is done by the mothers of the children who are a part of an also award winning organisation, Parikrma Humanity Foundation in Bangalore. Many parents are small-scale tailors who have faced significant hardships as a result of the recent pandemic. Retailing 30 sets of coffee filters a month allows us to support an entire household. The cloth filters are a part of Parikrma's community development programme for parents whose livelihoods have been affected by the recent pandemic. How to Use Cloth filters can be washed and reused multiple times (but not for eternity!). To get the best use from them, first rinse a few times with hot water before you begin to brew. Once you are done, you can rinse again with hot water and hang to air dry. Do not wring or squeeze dry as it might change the shape. These filters may shrink in size over time, we have tried to factor this in but

Name: Bird-Friendly Bundle
Tasting_Notes: From sweet citrus to chocolate! INCLUDES Jumping Ant: Light
Desc: Why, Birds! The Bird-Friendly Bundle celebrates one of the most successful vertebrate groups on Earth—birds! Known for their feathers, beaks, and wings, birds are the only surviving relatives of the ancient Archosaurs, alongside crocodilians.
